engagement_title: Lanternwood Folk Fest programme: turn a bill of fourteen acts and fourteen photographs from fourteen different hands into one keepsake booklet, working from two old printed pages that do not convert the way they look
vertical: Arts, culture and live music, a two day roots and Americana festival on a working farm in Somerset, England, ticketed at sixty five pounds a day, run by a six person volunteer committee
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, 'Event Program Booklet / Brochure Design': a client producing a booklet style brochure that will double as the official program guide, asking for careful proofreading, alignment and image optimisation for print, a press ready PDF, and every logo crisp, proportionate and consistently placed with plenty of white space so partners look their best. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional Lanternwood Folk Fest; no real festival, venue, artist, company or trademark appears anywhere. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept and the collateral and deepens it to standard. The repositioning the ledger already flagged holds under CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10): the booklet is a genuine record per page variable data run built out of the committee's own printed pages rather than a free composition, the per performer photograph genuinely binds per record, and the festival crest is recovered off a photograph of the painted stage banner rather than redrawn.
client_one_liner: Fourteen acts, fourteen photographs sent in by fourteen different people, two old printed programme pages and a spreadsheet, and the booklet has to be at the printer in eleven days.
client_brief:
Lanternwood Folk Fest, programme booklet

We are a volunteer committee running a two day roots and Americana festival on a farm outside Wells. Two stages, fourteen acts, tickets at sixty five pounds a day. The programme is the thing people keep. Ours end up pinned to kitchen walls, and last year we heard about it for months because we got the set times wrong on one page.

What we need is the booklet: a page for every act on the bill, with their photograph, their stage, their day and set time, and their own words about themselves. It has to run in the order the weekend actually runs in, so someone standing in a field can find the act that is about to go on.

What we can give you. Our old designer moved to Canada. We have two pages he printed for us, one from last year and one from two years before, and the printer's cover from last year. Use whichever of the two page designs works better; we like the newer one but we are not precious.

We have the line up sheet with everyone's stage, day, time and the biography they sent us. The photographs came from the acts themselves. Some are from a proper photographer, some are a phone at a gig, and they look nothing like each other, which is the part we cannot fix ourselves.

Our crest is on the painted banner over the main gate. We have never had it as a file. We would love it on every page and big on the two day boards we hang at each stage entrance, and we would like those boards as something we can edit next year, because the times always change.

At sixty five pounds a day people expect something that feels made. Please tell us anything you find that we should know before it goes to print.
price_band_and_audience: A ticketed sixty five pounds a day roots festival with a two thousand capacity, audience broadly thirty to sixty, many of them regulars who keep the programme. The band is load-bearing. At this price the booklet is a keepsake: photographs given real room, editorial type with a proper hierarchy, generous margins, one act per page breathing rather than filled. Take it down to the free town fair register (single colour, dense, photographs shrunk to thumbnails to save a page) and the ticket buyer feels the difference immediately, as the committee already heard about the set times. Push it up into the boutique arts biennale register (near empty pages, tiny type, no set times visible at speed) and it stops working as the thing someone standing in a field uses to find the next act, which is its only functional job. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when the merge is perfect. A posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 pounds fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Two days of roots on the farm
brand_identity.sector: A ticketed two day roots and Americana music festival, staged on a working farm and run by a volunteer committee.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small two stage festival on a farm outside Wells, Somerset, England, two thousand capacity, run by a six person volunteer committee.
brand_identity.about: Lanternwood is a roots and Americana weekend that people come back to year after year, held in a field with two stages and fourteen acts across two days. The programme is the keepsake: many end up pinned to a kitchen wall. The festival is proudly homemade but takes its craft seriously, because the ticket price asks it to.
brand_identity.audience: A roots and Americana crowd broadly thirty to sixty, many of them returning regulars who keep the programme, willing to pay for something that feels made rather than mass produced.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Sixty five pounds a day. A considered keepsake register: photographs given real room, editorial type with a proper hierarchy, generous margins, one act to a page breathing rather than a dense fair handout, and never a near empty boutique arts brochure.
brand_identity.typography: A keepsake editorial pairing: a warm serif for act names and headings with a clean, legible sans or serif for set times, stage and biographies. Readable at a glance in a field, generous in a programme, with a clear hierarchy so a reader finds the next act quickly.
brand_identity.voice: Friendly, plain and a little handmade, the voice of a committee that runs the thing itself. Example line the brand would write: "Grab a pint, find your stage, and we will see you down the front."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No working files survive. The previous designer moved to Canada, leaving only two printed programme pages held by the printer (last year's and the year before) plus last year's printed cover. The crest has never existed as a file: it lives only as paint on the canvas banner over the main gate, photographed for reference. Fonts and colours must be inferred from the printed pages.
brand_identity.values: The programme is the keepsake, and the crest is how regulars recognise the festival. Both should feel handmade but properly made, worthy of the wall they end up on.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_programme_2025_pages.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages from last year's printed programme, held by the printer: the cover and one performer profile page, real embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's programme. We like this one better, it looks more like us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The profile page's portrait was flattened into the page by the old designer rather than placed, so the converted document exposes no graphic frame at all and there is nothing for a per performer photograph to bind to, however obviously the printed page shows a photograph. The stage line, the set time and the biography also sit inside one continuous flow, so they cannot be addressed as separate frames. None of this is visible from the printed page and the conversion reports no problem.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_programme_2023_page.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: One performer profile page from the programme two years ago, a plainer design by the same person before he changed his layout.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The older one. Less handsome, but we included it in case it helps."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: This is the page that actually works, because its portrait is a genuinely placed image and its blocks are separated, but its portrait frame is close to square and considerably smaller than the printed page suggests, while the press photographs are wide stage frames. The biography frame is also set tight to that year's shorter biographies and does not spill or reflow, so a longer biography stops rendering partway and ends mid sentence at trim while the merge reports every record complete.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_press_photos/ (14 frames, from 14 different sources)
assets_supplied.kind: One photograph per act, supplied by the acts themselves: some from a commissioned shoot, some grabbed at a gig on a phone, one saved off a band's own website.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The photographs the acts sent us. They look nothing like each other and we know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two are stage captures under a heavy magenta wash where a global correction toward the set's neutral takes the skin green rather than neutral. Two more put the performer in a narrow lit band against a black stage, so a subject focused crop locks onto a lit stand or a monitor wedge and returns a confident looking frame that clips the face, reporting its uncertainty only as a detection confidence number and a detection box in the metadata. One arrives already sharpened and heavily saturated by somebody's phone preset, so it fights any correction applied on top of it.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_banner_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the painted canvas banner over the main gate, the crest on it in two paints on weathered cream canvas: a lantern with glazing bars inside a laurel ring, under an arched wordmark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our crest. It has only ever existed as paint on that banner."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound painted mark on a weathered substrate. A prompt naming the banner returns the canvas. A prompt naming the whole crest returns the arched wordmark and silently drops the lantern and the laurel ring while looking entirely plausible. Background removal on the laurel ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The paint has also spread into the canvas weave, so the glazing bars and the gaps between the laurel leaves carry far less separation than they appear to at full frame.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Fourteen rows: act name, stage, day, set time, the biography the act sent in, and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone's stage, day, time and the words they sent us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rows sit in the order the acts were booked, which is neither day order nor set time order, and row order is exactly what determines page order in the finished booklet. The biographies are also wildly uneven because each act wrote its own: the shortest is two sentences and three of them run to nearly double the longest of last year's.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_committee_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the committee: ticket price, the two stage names, which two acts are the headliners and must not be sequenced as though they are not, the licence line that must appear, and the printer's deadline.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything else you need to know from us."

acceptance_bar: One press file whose page count is exactly the number of acts on the bill, in the order the weekend actually runs, so that someone standing in a field can find the act about to go on.
Every page carries that act's own photograph. One face repeated, or an act paired with another act's photograph, is a total failure of the booklet.
Every biography ends in a finished sentence at trim. A biography that cannot be set in full is fitted or flagged to us in writing, never left stopping in the middle.
Every field the page shows actually lands in the template. A template that reports success while holding fewer fields than the page displays is a failed template, however clean the report reads.
The fourteen photographs read as one booklet rather than fourteen sources: one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame, and every face whole and correctly placed in its frame.

The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable, no opaque rectangle riding underneath it, and still legible as a lantern inside a laurel ring at the size it actually prints on a profile page, not merely at full canvas.
A cover proof at true print resolution, not a screen sized render enlarged to look like one.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no crop report in the run carries an upscale entry.

The two day boards are one working file we can edit next year, each at its own size, with live text and the crest as real shapes rather than a picture of a layout, and both boards readable at the distance a stage entrance is read from.
What can and cannot honestly be promised to the printer about trim and bleed from pages of this origin is stated plainly in writing.

The written note tells us what we could not have known: what our own pages do when they convert, what our photographs do at page size, what our biographies do to the layout, and anything about the crest we should be careful with.

Two candidate printed pages are converted and their true frame inventories read out of the round tripped IDML, one is chosen on structural grounds rather than on how it looks, a mapping is authored against reconstructed story text, placeholders are written and re-verified, and the bill is merged one act per page in running order. The same surface renders the cover proof at real print resolution, which the merge cannot produce.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier and the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, then upload every supplied asset and hold each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: A page per act at volume is variable data work against a real document; the day boards are a fixed canvas composition the committee edits next year. The merge binds images by exact filename, so the manifest is what keeps a photograph attached to an act once fourteen frames have been through five operations each.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming a surface per deliverable, the confirmed tier that gates the export, and a manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Convert both candidate profile pages into live documents, export the IDML of each, and read what each conversion actually produced: text frame count, graphic frame count, bounds and proportions, applied faces and sizes.
trajectory.judgement: The committee chose between the two pages by looking at them, which is the wrong basis and the only one they had. What matters is what each conversion exposes as addressable, which has nothing to do with which page is handsomer.
trajectory.produces: Two true frame inventories side by side, with the portrait frame's real proportion where one exists.

trajectory.action: On the page that can carry the job, ask for the mapping readout against the line up sheet, then reconstruct the frame's true story text from the document's own content runs and compute every offset from that reconstruction.
trajectory.judgement: The readout is a convenience, not a source of truth, and offsets computed from it validate cleanly whether or not they are right. The document's own content runs are the only text that exists.
trajectory.produces: A mapping authored against reconstructed story text, with each field's action and position.

trajectory.action: Decide the running order from the sheet's stage, day and time columns and the committee's note about the headliners, and re-sort the sheet into that order.
trajectory.judgement: Row order is page order and the sheet arrived in booking order. Two parallel stages make running order an editorial choice rather than a sort: strict chronology interleaves the stages, grouping by stage breaks chronology, and the test is someone standing in a field looking for the next act.
trajectory.produces: The bill in a defended running order, with the ordering rule written down.

trajectory.action: Recover the crest off the banner: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's returned box, a trace, a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed, then a print size plate derived from the same chain for the merge to bind.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes paint rather than canvas, which polarity to trace, and what to do about a compound mark whose parts do not all come back from one prompt. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed laurel ring. The crest has to exist before the template is prepared, because it reaches the printed page as a bound image rather than as something that can be placed by hand.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest, a colour accurate variant, and the print size plate the profile pages bind.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen photographs and triage them: which are stage captures, which carry a heavy colour wash, which put the subject in a narrow lit band, which arrived already processed, which are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen sources is not fourteen problems of the same kind, and sorting them before touching any of them prevents one correction being applied to a frame that needs the opposite.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast and prior processing.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, fix one booklet target from the strongest frame, and bring each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, confining the correction to the material it belongs to where a whole frame move goes wrong.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a booklet, not fourteen good photographs, and frames under a colour wash cannot reach it by the route the daylight ones take. Prompt wording is the whole gate on a confined correction, since naming the object pulls the selection to the object.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Crop each master to the chosen template's real portrait proportion with the face placed rather than centred, reading what each crop reports about how it found its subject, and name each file to the value the sheet's image column carries.
trajectory.judgement: The proportion comes from the converted document, not the printed page. On a stage frame the brightest thing is often not the performer, and a crop that reports success is not evidence that it found a face.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen named portrait files at or below source scale, each with its detection reading recorded.

trajectory.action: Write the placeholders into the chosen document with the mapping passed as a single stringified object, binding both image frames (the portrait varying per record, the crest constant across the bill), then export the IDML again and confirm by inspection that every expected field is present.
trajectory.judgement: Preparation reports success whether or not the mappings landed, and a booklet missing its set times is the exact failure the committee already lived through once. One of the two image columns genuinely is constant and the other must vary, which is the opposite of the usual mistake.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template with a written field by field confirmation.

trajectory.action: Merge the re-sorted bill against the template with the fourteen portraits and the crest plate supplied as additional image files bound to their columns, taking the result as one press file.
trajectory.judgement: The image column is the difference between a programme and fourteen copies of one page, and the running order decided before any page was set is what the printer will bind.
trajectory.produces: One multi page press file, one act per page, each carrying its own photograph.

trajectory.action: Read every page of the merged booklet: each biography to its end, each set time against the sheet, each face against the act, and each crest at the size it actually prints on the page.
trajectory.judgement: A merge that completes tells you the mechanism ran. The acts who wrote the most about themselves, and the crest at its smallest, will not announce themselves in any response.
trajectory.produces: A page by page read with every defective record and every reproduction problem named.

trajectory.action: Render the cover at true print resolution from the converted cover page, and confirm the delivered raster is genuinely at that resolution rather than a screen sized page enlarged.
trajectory.judgement: The merge surface silently ignores a resolution request, so a print proof has to come from the render surface, and believing the requested number rather than the delivered file is how a soft cover reaches a printer.
trajectory.produces: A cover proof at real print resolution with its dimensions recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name and build one kit; then license one camera scale evening field and marquee frame on short generic queries, photography only, generative candidates excluded.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a sixty five pound keepsake and a reader standing in a field, and weight cannot be inferred from a style name. A licensed frame that does not join fourteen real performance photographs reads as bought.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and weight per role, plus one licensed IP clean frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document holding the two day boards at board scale, each root declaring its own canvas, the licensed band and every photograph carried as image data, the crest as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A stage entrance board is read at distance and at speed, so the schedule's structure is the design problem. A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying both boards, retained as a durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check and export, verifying through both available channels (the document's rendition for the first board, the returned per root markup for the second), then create the committee's selects board within the per call placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard, so looking at board one is not looking at the deliverable. A partial board result is partial, and vector artwork belongs in the note rather than on the board.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document verified across both boards, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the committee's two printed pages can actually carry this job. Both plainly show a performer photograph. What one of them exposes on conversion is no graphic frame at all, because that photograph was flattened into the page rather than placed, so there is nothing for a per act photograph to bind to, and its text was set as one continuous flow so stage, time and biography cannot be addressed separately. The other, which the committee likes less, exposes a genuinely placed image frame and separated blocks, but at a portrait proportion that has nothing to do with what the printed page suggests. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under anyone's control, appears in no error, and the unusable page converts exactly as cleanly as the usable one.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the inventory does not exist until the conversion has run, and there is no parameter that requests placed images or separated blocks. Doing it right first time would mean already knowing which of two visually similar pages hides a flattened photograph. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the committee prefers the newer page and is not precious, which is an aesthetic preference rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the outcome is a different template, a different mapping strategy and a different portrait proportion for all fourteen photographs.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Convert and inspect the second candidate rather than proceeding on the preferred one, choose on structural grounds, tell the committee why the page they liked cannot carry a per act photograph, and re-derive the portrait crop specification for all fourteen frames from the chosen template's real bounds.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A fourteen page booklet in which every act's page shows the same flattened face from last year's programme, delivered after a conversion, a validation, a preparation and a merge that all reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered crest survives at the size it is actually printed. The trace looks correct at full canvas, with lantern, glazing bars, laurel ring and arched wordmark all present and separated. On the profile page the crest sits small on a cream ground, and the paint's spread into the banner's weave means the glazing bars and the gaps between the laurel leaves carry far less separation than they appear to at full frame, so at reproduction size the counters close and the mark reads as a dark blob with a ring around it. The tracing tool takes no options at all, so nothing can be tuned after the fact, and no readout reports path density against reproduction size. It exists only once the page is rendered at print resolution and looked at at true size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: all tuning has to happen in the raster preparation before the trace, and whether this particular painted mark on this particular weave holds at this particular size cannot be known before both the trace and the page exist. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the crest on every page and big on the boards, which is a placement wish rather than a warning about small reproduction. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different upstream chain, a re-selected and re-cropped raster or a deliberately simplified single weight variant for small use.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation, re-select the paint at a tighter crop and cleaner polarity, re-trace, and judge at printed size on the cream ground rather than at full canvas; where it still closes, produce a distinct small use variant and state which variant is for which size. The boards are then re-authored around whichever crest is now correct.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen keepsake pages and two stage boards carrying a crest that is a dark blob at page size, on a festival whose crest has only ever existed as paint and is the thing regulars recognise it by.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the constructions the day boards are built on. A stage entrance board is a schedule read at distance, and the natural authoring of that is a multi column running order with the crest lifted off a photographic band. The importer silently discards multi column text and reflows it into a single column, and it discards the effects that separate a mark from a photograph behind it, all at full success with no warning of any kind. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the second board cannot be checked that way at all, and the returned per root markup is the only channel that reports what survived. Whether the board still reads as a schedule at twenty paces exists only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for boards the committee can edit and that read at a stage entrance, which is a functional wish. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a structurally different authoring of the same board, explicitly laid out sibling containers rather than a flowed one, and a crest separated from its band by a solid panel rather than by an effect.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Audit the returned markup for both roots rather than looking at the first board, re-author the schedule as explicitly positioned sibling blocks, re-seat the crest on a construct that survives, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export and audit both roots again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two stage entrance boards delivered as an editable file in which the running order has collapsed into one column and the crest has disappeared into the photograph, on the one deliverable nobody can check by opening the first page.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood programme, press booklet and cover proof
deliverables.spec: One press file whose page count equals the number of acts on the bill, one act per page, in a defended running order, each page carrying that act's own photograph, its own stage, day and set time, and its own biography ending in a finished sentence at trim. Delivered with a cover proof rendered at true print resolution, and with the running order rule written down.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood performer photography, normalised
deliverables.spec: Fourteen photographs from fourteen sources brought to one booklet look (one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame), cropped to the chosen template's real portrait proportion with the face placed rather than centred and whole in every frame, named to the values the line up sheet binds by, with no output above the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from. Delivered with a per frame parameter log naming why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Recovered Lanternwood crest
deliverables.spec: The compound crest recovered from a photograph of a painted banner as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque rectangle riding underneath, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, still reading as a lantern inside a laurel ring at the size it actually prints on a profile page as well as at board scale, with the small use variant identified as such if one proves necessary.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood stage entrance day boards
deliverables.spec: One native editable document holding both day boards at board scale, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the crest as real vector shapes, the licensed band and any photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and a running order that survives the import as a readable schedule. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the committee edits the boards next year when the times change.

deliverables.name: Printer note, mapping record and committee board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording which of the two supplied pages was used and why in structural terms, the template's real frame inventory and the field mapping as finally verified, the running order rule, every biography that had to be fitted or flagged, every reduction or enlargement any tool reported, the type used by role with family, foundry and numeric weight, what can and cannot honestly be promised about trim and bleed, and which crest variant is for which size. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press file's page count equals the number of acts, and page order matches the delivered running order document exactly.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the PDF page count against the line up row count, then read the act name on each page and compare the sequence against the stated running order.

verifiers_auto.text: The prepared template contains every field the profile page carries, not a subset.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the IDML of the prepared template and grep the stories for every expected placeholder token, asserting the full set is present.

verifiers_auto.text: Every page's photograph is distinct and matches the act named on that page.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the embedded images page by page, hash them, assert fourteen distinct hashes, and check each page's hash against its row's image value.

verifiers_auto.text: The cover proof is genuinely at print resolution rather than a screen sized page enlarged.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the delivered raster's pixel dimensions and embedded density against the page's physical trim size.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered raster exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file's dimensions against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered crest's SVG carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox attribute exists and that the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The board export returned two roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with no image resolved to the importer's placeholder and the crest present as vector path shapes on both.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and per slide dimensions from the export response, then parse the returned per root markup for placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the crest region on each root.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default, and the schedule block survives as more than one positioned container.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and count the positioned sibling blocks in the schedule region.

verifiers_human.text: Every biography ends where a sentence ends, at trim, including the three longest ones.
verifiers_human.how: Read the biography block on every page of the press file at trim size, with attention to the longest rows in the sheet.

verifiers_human.text: The fourteen photographs read as one booklet rather than fourteen sources, and every face is whole and correctly placed in its frame.
verifiers_human.how: Flip the booklet at reading pace, then lay the fourteen crops side by side and judge white point, contrast, head size and placement as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The crest reads as a lantern inside a laurel ring at the size it prints on a profile page, not only at board scale.
verifiers_human.how: View the printed page at true size on the cream ground and look at the crest's counters and laurel gaps.

verifiers_human.text: Someone standing in a field can find the act about to go on.
verifiers_human.how: Give the booklet and a stage entrance board to a reader with a day and a time and see how long it takes them, then read the boards at the distance a stage entrance is read from.

verifiers_human.text: The booklet reads as a sixty five pound a day keepsake rather than a free fair handout or a boutique arts brochure.
verifiers_human.how: Judge photograph weight, margin, type hierarchy and page density against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the committee something they did not already know, including anything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and confirm the template decision, every fitted biography and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Which of the two supplied printed pages can actually carry a per act photograph, decided on what each conversion exposes rather than on which page the committee prefers, and how to tell them so.
Whether to author the mapping against the readout's convenient string or against the document's own reconstructed text.
The running order of the booklet: strict chronology interleaves two parallel stages, grouping by stage breaks chronology, and the headliners cannot be sequenced as though they are not.
The portrait crop proportion, set by the chosen template's real frame bounds rather than by what either printed page appears to show.

Which of the two image bindings varies and which is constant across the bill, given that binding both the same way produces either fourteen identical faces or fourteen missing crests, and both merge cleanly.
Per frame correction strategy across fourteen sources, including which frames cannot reach the booklet target by a whole frame move and need the correction confined to the material it belongs to.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on a stage frame where the brightest thing is not the performer, or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection.
Per act copy fitting on the longest biographies: what can be cut from words an act wrote about itself, and what has to go back to the committee instead.

Selection wording on the banner: naming the banner takes the canvas, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the crest, and background removal on an enclosed laurel ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which crest variant carries the profile page, judged at printed size on the cream ground rather than at full canvas, and whether a distinct small use variant is needed at all.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a sixty five pound keepsake and a reader standing in a field.
How much room the photographs get. At this band generosity is the design, and a dense page that fits everything in is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a festival programme page. IDENTITY: these are fourteen real acts whose own photographs and own words have to appear on their own pages, and the crest has to be RECOVERED off a photograph of the painted banner the audience recognises the festival by, because a regenerated crest is a different festival's crest. SPEC: the booklet's page count must equal the bill, the pages must run in the order the weekend runs, every act must carry its own photograph and its own set time, and the cover proof must be at real print resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the day boards exist because the times change every year and the committee explicitly intends to edit them itself. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this page convert into something that can hold a photograph, does this biography end in a sentence, does this crest still read at the size it prints.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: the full convert, export_idml, mapping, prepare, merge and render chain is verified fully headless and synchronous, including building a live merge template from a bare PDF, with page count equal to row count for PDF output and per row image binding through an @ prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles visually confirmed. The first checkpoint rests on the documented finding that FRAME GRANULARITY FROM A PDF IS NOT UNDER YOUR CONTROL: a continuous text flow converted to exactly one TextFrame and ZERO graphic frames, while a source carrying real placed images converted to two text frames plus two graphic frames, with no error either way. The cover proof rests on two further findings: outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is SILENTLY IGNORED (a 300 request returned 72 DPI) while document_render_layout at resolution 300 returned a true 2550x3300 raster at 300x300 density. The lossy textContent trap (a dropped run leaving every later offset short, with the validator returning VALID and prepare reporting success while mappings failed to land) is live and is why the mapping is authored from reconstructed content runs. IMAGING: straighten, masked and unmasked adjustments, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and vectorize are verified across 27 live calls; the substrate versus paint prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure on an enclosed ring, image_vectorize taking NO OPTIONS AT ALL so all tuning happens in the raster prep, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export and inline SVG as native editable vector are verified, column-count is documented as DROPPED with the text reflowing to a single column, filter blur and text-shadow are dropped, multi layer box-shadow truncates to layer one, and the rendition preview is first artboard only. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end; short Stock queries only with orientation never passed; boards capped at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim from a PDF sourced template, no pdfPreset, no naming of per record raster outputs by position, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20 files.
